Abstract
This paper emphasizes the integration of wind and photovoltaic (PV) generation with
battery energy storage systems (BESS) in distribution networks (DNs) to enhance grid
sustainability, reliability, and ﬂexibility. A novel multi-objective optimization framework is
introduced in this study to minimize energy supply costs, emissions, and energy losses
while improving voltage deviation (VD) and voltage stability index (VSI). The proposed
framework comprising normal boundary intersection (NBI) and decomposition-based
evolutionary algorithms (DBEA) determines the optimal siting and sizing of renewable-
based distributed resources, considering load demand variations and the intermittency of
wind and solar outputs. The comparative analysis establishes that the proposed strategy
performs better than many contemporary algorithms, speciﬁcally when all the objective
functions are optimized simultaneously. The validation of the proposed framework was
carried out on the standard IEEE-33 bus test network, which demonstrates signiﬁcant
percentage savings in energy supply costs (49.6%), emission rate (62.2%), and energy loss
(92.3%), along with enormous improvements in VSI (91.9%) and VD (99.8953%). The
obtained results categorically underline the efﬁciency, reliability, and robustness of the pro-
posed approach when employed on any complex distribution network comprising multiple
renewable energy sources and battery storage systems.
1 INTRODUCTION
1.1 Background, scope, and challenges
Massive carbon emissions are wreaking havoc around the
world. Global warming and climate change have been making
the lives of humans very difﬁcult, and their impacts are seen
in the shape of rapid glaciers melting, rising temperatures, and
increasing turbulences in aircraft. The major cause of these
hazards is burning fossil fuels; hence, it is imperative to shift
traditional power systems to renewable energy sources com-
pletely. The abundant energy can be exploited through solar,
wind, and water-based power generators. Distributed resources
(DR) power systems are not directly connected to a bulk power
transmission system; nonetheless, they include both distributed
generations (DGs) and battery energy storage systems (BESS)
which are vital components in the current development of

modern power systems [ 1]. Their collective impact on sus-
tainability, reliability, and ﬂexibility aligns seamlessly with the
broader objectives of transitioning towards cleaner and more
resilient energy infrastructures. As technological evolutions
enhance, the critical roles played by DG and BESS are expected
to expand, contributing signiﬁcantly to a more sustainable
and adaptive energy landscape [ 2, 3 ]. Due to the increasing
demand for electricity and alarmingly rapid fossil fuel depletion,
alternative energy sources have gained enormous attention
in recent decades. Consequently, research into integrating
distributed generations with distribution networks (DNs) has
received extensive attention [ 4]. Furthermore, placing a DG in
the best location with a suitable size can mitigate the necessity
of reactive power to improve the voltage proﬁle and reduce
active power losses. Numerous researchers have proposed mul-
tiple optimization strategies to solve the formulated problems,
which include conventional, artiﬁcial intelligence, and hybrid

Previously carried out studies on the optimal DGs’ integra-
tion in the distribution networks have only focused on the
minimization of power losses and included a single objective
function employing analytical approaches in [ 6], heuristic and
meta-heuristic methods that comprise genetic algorithm [ 7], ant
lion optimization algorithm [ 8], and mixed integer non-linear
programming [9]. The recent research involves several objective
functions to optimize DG siting and sizing, including higher
voltage stability and reduced operational and carbon dioxide
emissions costs. Genetic algorithm-based methods BSOA [ 10]
a n dG A[11], computational methods ICA [12], MNLP [13], and
ALOA [ 9], and hybrid optimization methods Fuzzy [ 14], and
HPSO [ 15] are employed to achieve the projected outcomes.
Nevertheless, these approaches suffer heavily while optimizing
multiple objective functions simultaneously, and the usage
of weighted aggregation also makes the objective functions
consume a long time to solve the problem and obtain desired
solutions. In the next attempt, Pareto optimality is employed
to solve the optimization problems with various objective func-
tions. Given that the multiple objective functions are optimized
uniformly, the Pareto optimality techniques yield Pareto sets
of the best solutions to achieve optimal results. However, the
primary method only generates a single outcome whenever the
value of each objective is selected. Recent studies have exploited
multi-objective evolutionary algorithms based on the Pareto
optimality concept to ﬁnd the optimal locations and sizing of
DGs comprising NSGAII [ 16], INSGAII [ 17], IMOHS [ 18],
MOShBAT [ 7], and non-dominated sorting stochastic fractal
search (NSSFS) [ 19], in an attempt to avoid limitation. These
employed evolutionary algorithms (EAs) render a choice of
Pareto-optimal solutions from which the network can make a
fair decision. The integration of multiple distributed genera-
tions simultaneously is typically analysed individually. However,
combining these two sub-problems will be a better choice for
the whole power system. Most authors optimize a single objec-
tive function to minimize power loss in distributed networks.
Researchers in [ 20–22] pointed out that a minimal amount of
power loss was found when the multiple DGs were combined
and optimized to ﬁnd an optimal solution. However, a few
researchers have attempted to optimize such complex problems
with additional objectives. In [ 23], the authors employed fuzzy-
ACO (ant colony optimization) based on Pareto optimality on
a single solar-based DG and DSTATCOM to ﬁnd their opti-
mal locations and sizes aimed to minimize active power loss,
increase feeder loading balance balancing, and improve the volt-
age proﬁle of the system. Since the above-discussed approaches
evaluated the weighted sum of the objective functions, the
Pareto optimality could not optimize the objective functions
evenly. Hitherto, deliberate research studies treated the DG
models as deterministic; however, practically, they are highly
intermittent and volatile; speciﬁcally, distribution generations
based on renewable energy. Most previously discussed literature
focused on the optimal placement of distributed generations for
a single period only. The allocation of renewable energy-based
DGs is central in distribution networks because these DGs
are environmentally friendly, reduce losses, enhance economic
growth, and are free from generating greenhouse gases (GHG).
Hence, accepting their immense signiﬁcance and beneﬁts,
societies and utility companies strive towards cleaner and more
resilient energy systems. However, the described energy sources
are highly intermittent and unpredictable and lead to several
scheduling problems; the employment of battery energy storage
systems (BESSs) assists in tackling the challenges caused by the
intermittency of the renewable energy sources and demand and
supply mismatches in the power network.
1.2 Literature review, contributions, and
structure of the paper
Battery energy storage systems are essential in managing and
optimizing the utilization of renewable energy in distribution
networks. They guarantee a steady and reliable power supply by
storing surplus energy throughout a high-generation period and
discharging it during a demand span. It reduces power varia-
tions, keeps grid stability, and plummets the necessity for costly
power sources. Battery energy storage systems support power
systems in emergencies and variations by enhancing power qual-
ity and supplying auxiliary power. Through this action, the
effectiveness and reliability of renewable energy are improved,
which leads to tangible economic beneﬁts. An all-inclusive com-
parison of the proposed algorithm with the latest research
studies is shown in Table 1.
Table 1 expounds a wide-ranging approach to the proposed
algorithm, optimizing several objective functions together,
which are solved for the ﬁrst time, and such analysis does not
exist in the literature review . The proposed algorithm success-
fully integrates distributed resources (DRs) comprising both
distributed generation (DG) and battery energy storage sys-
tems (BESS). It solves all the objective functions simultaneously
to achieve optimal solutions involving both deterministic and
probabilistic methodologies in single-period and multi-period
scenarios. The proposed framework effectively solves the for-
mulated objective functions, that is, the cost of energy supplied
(C), emission rate (E), energy loss reduction (CEL), voltage
stability index (VSI), and voltage deviation (VD). In a compara-
tive analysis, the results of the employed technique outperform
many contemporary optimization algorithms by solving com-
plex challenges related to distribution networks and validating
their efﬁciency and superiority. Henceforth, this study makes
massive contributions by signiﬁcantly ﬁlling the research gap
by solving ﬁve critical conﬂicting objective functions to opti-
mize distributed resource allocation in a complex distribution
network. According to the authors’ best knowledge, a novel
framework is introduced in this paper, which proposes a uni-
ﬁed strategy to solve the multiple conﬂicting objective functions
together in a multi-period time frame, which does not exist in
the previous research works.
The presented study focuses on the critical role of renew-
able energy-based DGs and BESS integration and optimization
in enhancing the economic and environmental performance of
distribution networks. It introduces a dynamic, multi-objective
framework to address the problems renewable energy sources

The allocation of distributed resources is a multi-objective
mixed integer non-linear problem. It poses a challenge to the
existing multi-objective evolutionary algorithms due to their
small feasible search space and constraints in both objective
and control variables space. To address this lacuna, this paper
proposes an improved decomposition-based evolutionary algo-
rithm (I-DBEA) employed with the epsilon constraint method
to handle constraints and solve highly complex multi-objective
problems.

The multi-objective evolutionary algorithms aim to ﬁnd high-
quality, non-dominated (ND) solutions in a simulation run. The
quality measurement of the ND solutions has three goals, that
is, convergence (minimum distance between the ideal point
and PF), diversity (uniform distribution), and maximum spread,
which should be considered while assessing the performance of
MOEAs. The ﬁnal obtained non-dominated MOEA solutions
must have maximum convergence, diversity, and spread. Sev-
eral criteria have been proposed to compare the performance
of MOEAs precisely. This study measures the convergence and
diversity of MOEAs using the hypervolume indicator (HVI)
performance technique. In the HVI metric, a reference point
(ideally around the nadir point) is obtained from the real PF ,
and no exact Pareto optimum solution exists in the real-world
DG and SC allocation problem. Due to the absence of the real
Pareto fronts, the exact nadir point remains to be determined.
The optimal and nadir locations are obtained by executing each
approach 20 times separately. Afterward, all the ND solutions
are combined, and dominated solutions are found via ND sort-
ing techniques [ 36]. The real Pareto optimum set combines the
ﬁltered set of ND solutions to carry out optimal and nadir val-
ues of MOEA. The best PF on a problem is the one with the
biggest HVI. Four DG and DG-SC study cases of small to large-
scale radial distribution systems with constant PQ load models

5 DISCUSSION
The presented study proposes the integration of wind and
PV-based DGs with BESS devices in a complex distribution
network. The study emphasizes the critical synergy between
DGs and BESS devices to enhance the sustainability, depend-
ability, and ﬂexibility of the power system, which are the key
elements to achieving a successful transition towards low-
carbon energy systems. A novel multi-objective optimization
framework is introduced in this paper to tackle many conﬂict-
ing objective functions, that is, cost of energy supplied, emission
rate, cost of energy loss, voltage stability index, and voltage
deviation simultaneously. The proposed framework integrates
normal boundary intersection and decomposition-based evo-
lutionary algorithms, efﬁciently solving the siting and sizing of
renewable-energy-based DGs and BESS devices. The proposed
system considers the load demand variations, intermittency, and
volatility of the renewable energy output. The standard IEEE 33
bus network was employed to validate the proposed algorithm.
The results found in the study are compelling and showcase
the signiﬁcant improvement made by the proposed algorithm
in enhancing the efﬁciency, environmental sustainability, and
reliability of the distribution network. The results show a sub-
stantial reduction in power losses, voltage deviations, cost of
energy supplied and energy loss, and emissions cost, along with
signiﬁcantly enhancing voltage stability.
When the results of the proposed algorithm are compared
with other algorithms, it establishes its superiority over them
throughout all cases, especially when multiple objectives are
optimized simultaneously. Henceforth, the framework under-
lines its ability to perform the optimal siting and sizing of
solar-type and wind-type DGs with BESS devices by reduc-
ing the need for grid station MV A capacity. The BESS devices
show their importance by optimizing renewable energy uti-
lization by stabilizing the grid and increasing the reliability of
the power supply. The results enormously contribute to the
ongoing research, making the distribution networks and smart
grids more efﬁcient and sustainable as they tackle economic,
environmental, and technical objective functions by integrat-
ing DGs based on renewable energy and BESS devices. The
accomplished research ﬁndings are thoroughly outlined in three
distinct scenarios as given:
Scenario 1: It focuses on the DGs with a constant PQ
load model, showing the capability of the proposed
algorithm in optimizing their optimal capacities and
locations. The presented cases validate the superior-
ity of the proposed algorithm in mitigating the cost
of energy supplies and energy loss, emission rates,
and voltage deviations while enhancing the voltage sta-
bility index when compared to other contemporary
algorithms considering both unity and lagging power
factors.
Scenario 2: This scenario broadens the scope of the study
by encompassing both DGs and SCs, underlining the
proposed algorithm’s ability to generate high-quality,
non-dominated solutions. The achieved results validate
the proposed algorithm’s superiority in terms of conver-
gence, diversity, and speed, emphasizing its robustness
across a wide spectrum of objective functions.

6 CONCLUSION
This paper aims to integrate solar and wind-type distributed
generators with battery energy storage systems simultaneously
in a complex distribution network to enhance the reliability
and ﬂexibility of power systems. A novel many-objective opti-
mization framework is introduced to solve multiple conﬂicting
objective functions by reducing the cost of energy supplied,
energy loss, voltage deviations, and emission rate while simul-
taneously enhancing the voltage stability index. The proposed
approach successfully determines the optimal siting and siz-
ing of the disturbed resources by exploiting improved normal
boundary intersection and decomposition-based evolutionary
techniques. The efﬁciency of the proposed algorithm is vali-
dated on the standard IEEE 33-bus network while considering
the intermittency in the output of renewable energy sources
and variations in load demand. The comparative analysis of the
proposed algorithm with other contemporary algorithms indi-
cates that it shows immense superiority over others in handling
ﬁve conﬂicting objective functions, simultaneously ensuring its
efﬁcacy by mitigating the need for capacity requirements from
the main station. The proposed framework achieved substan-
tial savings of 49.6%, 62.2%, and 92.3% in energy supply costs,
emission rate, and energy loss 92.3%, respectively, along with
enormous enhancements of 91.9% in voltage stability index and
99.8953% in voltage deviations compared to the base case study.
7 FUTURE WORK
Cutting-edge AI technologies can leverage the integration of
wind, solar, and battery energy storages for the optimal siting
and sizing of DERs, reducing energy losses and improving grid
stability. In future work, implementing advanced machine learn-
ing algorithms could enhance the prediction accuracy of renew-
able energy sources and load demand. The reinforcement learn-
ing algorithms could optimize the battery energy storage sys-
tems operation in real-time considering the dynamic grid condi-
tions. Moreover, the exploitation of deep learning frameworks
can analyse complex datasets to ﬁnd optimal locations for DGs
based on geographical, environmental, and grid constraints.
